subject: SierraBank - feature tradeoffs & contract dependency
messages:
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SierraBank - feature ask and contract consequence

Team — quick context up front: SierraBank (prospect) has moved to signature stage pending one last technical commitment. Procurement is asking us to commit in contract to two items that product/eng control:

1) Tenant-level routing (routing by customer tenancy + a failover variant) so they can route high-value transactions to an isolated execution lane.
2) On-demand audit export + one-year retention for audit logs tied to model inputs/outputs (they want an export endpoint and retention SLA).

They conditioned the commercial terms on this being deliverable within the next 6–8 weeks. Legal/procurement will not push forward without a delivery commitment. HubSpot deal HSP-87912 attached — mutual action plan attached (SierraBank_MutualActionPlan_v2.xlsx).

High-level ask to Product + Eng: can we (A) commit to a short-term shim that satisfies procurement within 4–6 weeks, or (B) commit to a full, durable feature (routing + export pipeline) and include realistic timeline/cost that we can put in the SOW?

Tradeoffs we should consider:
- Shim (fast): likely config + routing tags + temporary export job. Lower dev time, moderate operational fragility. Estimated incremental runrate impact ~+$12k–15k/mo (storage + ops).
- Full solution (long): tenant isolation primitives, export pipeline with retention controls, end-to-end QA and SOC2 evidence. More work (~10–12 weeks) and higher run costs (~+$30k/mo), but production-grade.

Security team will need to weigh in on export/PII scope; if we need additional encryption/KMS scope that will add time.

Asks:
- Ben: quick eng feasibility + ballpark estimates (scope and ETA) for shim vs full.
- Marissa: product decision on acceptable acceptance criteria for shim (what minimum guarantees do we give SierraBank).
- Laura: commercial / legal guidance on whether we can include phased delivery language and what level of credit/resolution SierraBank will accept if we miss a date.

I'm willing to take the customer call this afternoon if that helps get clarity.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SierraBank - feature ask and contract consequence

Thanks David — good summary. I think we can move quickly but we need concrete acceptance criteria and traffic/usage signals before committing. Quick questions:

- Expected steady qps and burst profile (P95/P99 expectations).
- Is this tied to particular model(s) or is it model-agnostic?
- Does SierraBank require export in a specific format (CSV, Parquet) + delivery to their storage?

Operationally I see two paths:
A) Interim shim (3–6 weeks): routing tags + per-tenant routing rules + an export job that dumps logs to a designated S3 and a small API to trigger/onboard exports. Minimal product features: config UI/flagging + documented limitations.
B) End-state (10–12 weeks): tenant isolation primitives, per-tenant export pipeline with retention controls, audit UI, accepted by Security for SOC2 scope.

For the shim I want the following acceptance criteria before we commit in writing:
- Export contains full request/response tokens for the specified retention period.
- We provide documented limitations (no guaranteed export throughput under extreme burst; best-effort availability).
- Canary plan: we must do a phased rollout with a pilot tenant and rollback plan.

Ben — can you run a quick feasibility + high-level capacity impact? If we can get a one-paragraph engineering risk summary + rough timeline today I can draft contract language that ties deliverables to an agreed mutual action plan.

Marissa
Product Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-12T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SierraBank - feature ask and contract consequence

Marissa / David / Laura — short scope + tradeoffs from engineering: see attached stub (eng_scope_rundown.pdf). TL;DR:

Interim shim (recommended if legal needs a date in the next 6 weeks):
- What it is: request tagging + routing policy + lightweight export job to push logs to customer S3. Will rely on current runtime; minimal kernel work.
- ETA: 3–5 weeks (including QA + canary).
- Run cost: incremental ~$12k/mo (S3 + export jobs + monitoring).
- Risks: not full tenant isolation — a noisy neighbor could still impact tail latency in edge cases; export pipeline is best-effort and we will need agreed SLA exclusions.

Full solution (durable):
- What it is: per-tenant routing lanes with dedicated capacity lanes, export + retention pipeline (Parquet), audit UI, KMS integration for encryption, and SOC2 acceptance evidence.
- ETA: 10–14 weeks (eng, infra, security reviews, QE).
- Run cost: incremental ~$30k+/mo.
- Risks: longer delivery, increased infra complexity, requires Security sign-off for KMS & retention.

Immediate asks for us to scope precisely:
1) SierraBank needs to share a realistic traffic forecast (sample of request sizes and qps during peak 30-minute windows).
2) Security questionnaire (we saw an initial set — need the complete one).
3) Confirmation on export format and destination (S3 credentials/permissions model).

If Product is comfortable with acceptance criteria listed by Marissa, Eng can produce an implementation plan with milestones and a canary gating checklist by EOD tomorrow.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime

Attachment: eng_scope_rundown.pdf (see stub)
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@sierrabank.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Steve Jenner <steve.jenner@sierrabank.com>, procurement@sierrabank.com
Date: 2028-07-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SierraBank - feature ask and contract consequence

Hi David / Marissa — appreciate the quick coordination. To be explicit from SierraBank procurement: the board wants a contractual commitment that the export + routing shim will be available and verifiable within 6 weeks. They are willing to accept a phased approach (shim first + full solution later) as long as there is a firm SOW and acceptance criteria.

We can provide the traffic sample and security questionnaire by end of day tomorrow. We are OK with the export being delivered to our S3 in Parquet. We also accept a canary pilot with our internal compliance team.

Two additional notes from procurement:
- We will include a modest financial holdback tied to final delivery of the full solution, but we need the first milestone (shim + export) committed in the MSA to secure internal sign-off.
- If Redwood can provide a 6-week delivery commitment for the shim with canary acceptance criteria and a defined escalation path, we will prioritize your contract for immediate signature.

Let me know windows for a 30-minute call tomorrow to align mutual action plan language. Steve (cc) will own procurement details.

Olivia Grant
VP, Digital Channels
SierraBank
